en.why: A slow drift followed by a fast gather contrasts speeds and gives a clear end point. The shape loses detail step by step, from a concrete product to geometry to a brand mark, while its position stays at the center of the frame without jumping. When the ending uses the same technique as the opening, the film closes on itself.
spec: Timing

Film 10.6s. Workspace demo 0–6.2s; the pieces drift down from 5.0s (1.2–1.5s, about 4–5% of frame height); converge from 6.2s: each piece starts 0–0.55s after 6.2s and takes 0.65–0.95s (20–29 frames); chrome leaves 6.2–6.7s, wallpaper washes to white 6.4–7.4s; mark lands 7.32s and settles over 0.65s (20 frames); wordmark pulls out 8.05–9.3s, tagline 8.9–9.7s, held to 10.6s
Easing

Drift linear; converge position on cubic-bezier(0.32,0,0.67,0) (power3.in, faster as they get closer) for one axis and power2.in for the other, so paths curve; scale power2.in, rotation power1.in, opacity fade power1.in over the last 35%; mark landing back.out(2.1); wordmark and tagline cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out)
Camera

Fixed frame, target icon at the center (960, 540). Slow push 1.00→1.035 linear over 0–6.2s (x −14px, y −6px), back to 1.0 over 6.2–7.1s with power2.inOut; after landing the lockup pushes 1.00→1.04 linear over 3.0s from 7.6s
Subject

17 pieces drift down, then gather on the center: 4 windows, a timer, a notification, a picture-in-picture, a command palette, 2 collaborator cursors, and 7 dock icons; they scale to 0.07–0.4, rotate 6–30° and fade out in their last 35%; the dock's own Tessel icon travels at full scale and the 200px mark takes over from it at the same size, leaving only the mark
Style

Light base #f5f5f7 under a pastel wallpaper (peach, pink, blue, lilac) that washes to white; white windows with 12px radius and soft violet shadows; indigo accent #5b5bf0 (icon gradient #8a8cff → #3d31d6) with four white tiles and one amber tile; faint violet vignette
en.prompt: Build an ending called Converge to Mark as a 10.6-second film. Build a product workspace on a light #f5f5f7 base with a pastel wallpaper: four white windows, a timer, a notification, a picture-in-picture, a command palette, two collaborator cursors, and a dock of 7 app icons with your icon in the middle; run a short demo for 6.2 seconds with a slow linear push (scale 1.00→1.035). From 5.0s drift every piece down at constant speed (34px per second). At 6.2s the menu bar and dock background leave over 0.5s, the wallpaper washes to white over 1.0s, and every piece travels to the center of the frame (960, 540): each starts 0–0.55 seconds after 6.2s and takes 0.65–0.95 seconds, with power3.in on one axis and power2.in on the other, scaling to 0.07–0.4 (windows 0.07–0.09), rotating 6–30° and fading out over the last 35%. The dock icon of your product travels at full scale and a 200px version takes over at the same size at 7.32s, landing with back.out(2.1) over 0.65 seconds with a glow ring behind it. At 8.05s the mark slides left while the wordmark is pulled out from behind it over 1.25 seconds with expo.out (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)), blur 10px→0, then the tagline fades in at 8.9s; push the lockup 4% and hold to 10.6s. Build it with HTML/SVG + GSAP.
says: Everything shrinks into one icon at the end
The scattered icons fly to the middle and become the logo
The text shrinks to a dot of light, then becomes the mark
vs: Converge to Mark gathers many elements to a point; Rotate to Lockup turns one object to a target angle.
The retract in Dispense Line-up only returns to the original subject; Converge to Mark ends on a new icon or logo.

body.h2: How to make a Converging Logo Reveal with Claude Code or Codex
body.body:
Start with a workspace demo of 17 pieces: 4 windows, a timer, a notification, a picture-in-picture, a command palette, 2 collaborator cursors and 7 dock icons. The pieces drift down 4–5% of frame height from 5.0s, then converge from 6.2s. Each starts 0–0.55s late and takes 0.65–0.95s on power3.in, so it speeds up near the center.

Scale the pieces to 0.07–0.4, rotate them 6–30° and fade them over their last 35%. The target is the frame center (960, 540). The 200px mark lands at 7.32s with back.out(2.1) and settles in 0.65s, the wallpaper washes to white 6.4–7.4s, and the wordmark pulls out over 8.05–9.3s on expo.out.

Press the copy button to send this recipe to Claude Code or Codex, or install the skill once with npx skills add krisyangdev/motionboard. The agent builds the 17 pieces and their converge paths. Render an MP4 with HyperFrames, or port the GSAP timeline to your website.

en.alt: Mail, task board, roadmap and calendar windows crowded on a desktop above the dock.
faq: What is a converging logo reveal?
A logo animation in which scattered elements move to one point and combine into the mark. The elements shrink and fade as they approach, so only the mark remains on screen.
Why accelerate the pieces as they converge?

Easing in with power3.in makes each piece faster as it nears the center, which gives the gather a clear end point after the slow drift. The paths curve because one axis uses power3.in and the other power2.in.

faq: 什么是汇聚式 logo 动画？
散开的多个元素移动到同一点，合成一个 logo。元素靠近时缩小、淡出，最后只剩标志。
为什么元素越靠近越快？
用 power3.in 缓入，元素靠近中心时加速，在缓慢漂移之后给汇聚一个明确的终点。一条轴用 power3.in、另一条轴用 power2.in，所以路径是弧线。
